en.title: Longest Contiguous Subarray Containing a High-Frequency Value
en.description:
Find the longest contiguous subarray in which at least one value occurs strictly more than the threshold k times. If none exists, output 0. The check here follows the statement's "strictly greater"; both of the original site's examples should give the full array length 7, and this site has corrected them.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤k≤n≤100000), and the second line contains n values (0..10⁹).
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: in the full array, 1 occurs 5 times, strictly more than the threshold 3, so the full length 7 is valid and optimal.
hints: Count frequencies over the whole array. If any frequency is greater than k, the whole array is optimal; otherwise no subarray can qualify.
